reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin by directing viewers to register, choose, and pay for a package while claiming they will profit regardless of whether they recommend it to others. It presents passive income and percentage bonuses tied to introducing people and multiple referral generations, reinforced by an earnings-plan slide showing direct sales, network, and matching bonuses. Millionaire claims and near-term growth language, together with instructions to secure a position and act now, create an easy-wealth and urgency framing.

opening.argument: Judge, the invitation leaves the viewer room to examine the offer before paying: it says to sign up for free, then choose a package, and points to further information about the compensation plan, packages, and company. It also invites questions through the person who introduced the viewer. Those steps do not validate the financial claims, but they matter when assessing whether the video asks for an immediate, uninformed payment. The speaker further says there are no recurring payments required to remain eligible to earn. The strongest concern is its sweeping profit claim; that claim should be scrutinized, not treated as proof that the described package and information are nonexistent.

citations.quote: sign up for free then decide which package you want to start off with and then make payment
Below this video, you will find more information explaining the compensation plan, packages and the company. If you have more questions contact the person who invited you here
There are no monthly payments to make in order to remain qualified to earn

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right to focus on the profit language, but it compresses a sequence into a demand to pay: the speaker first offers free registration and a choice of package. Its referral quotes establish advertised bonuses, not that every viewer must recruit to participate. The video expressly distinguishes recommending others from the package's stated mining component. None of that proves the offer sound; it does narrow what the cited statements establish.

citations.quote: sign up for free then decide which package you want to start off with and then make payment
your package includes the cost of mining for coins, so whatever happens you will profit from one coin even if you decide not to recommend us to others.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Free registration and an invitation to ask questions do not neutralize the payment request. The speaker directs viewers to choose a package and pay, then asserts that they will profit regardless of whether they recommend anyone. No recurring fee is required for a misleading paid offer to be promoted. The promised further information does not qualify the video's unconditional return claim.

opening.argument: Judge, substantial portions of this presentation explain a concept: the speaker introduces digital currency through the evolution of payment methods, then gives a simplified account of mining as computers running algorithms. The package discussion also identifies a training program and education packages. That material gives the viewer more than an unexplained request for money. The closing invitation is promotional, but the explanatory content is relevant to how the video should be read: it presents an account of a technology and an associated training offering, whose accuracy can be assessed separately from whether the presentation itself establishes a scam.

citations.quote: just think of it as the evolution of money

comprehensive training program called the one academy. You will learn exactly how to trade successfully and profit from digital currency with five education packages available

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's bonus and payment quotes are consequential, but they occur within a presentation that also explains what the speaker means by mining and describes training. The earnings-plan details show what the speaker says the program offers; they do not, by themselves, establish that the explanatory sections are a pretext or that the described training is absent. The video's promotional ending deserves weight without erasing its instructional content.

citations.quote: earlier I spoke about mining digital currency. So what does that mean?
comprehensive training program called the one academy.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technology explanation leads directly to a paid OneCoin offer. The training packages contain tokens to exchange for mining slots, and the closing instructs viewers to select a package and pay while promising profit whatever happens. Educational passages do not change the function of those claims: they support a solicitation built around paid mining and asserted returns.

citations.quote: five education packages available, all of which contain tokens which you can then exchange to buy mining slots for producing OneCoins
then make payment remember your package includes the cost of mining for coins, so whatever happens you will profit from one coin

opening.argument: Judge, the offer is described as a purchase with stated components: a trading package grants access to training, its tokens can be exchanged for mining slots, and the speaker says the package includes the cost of mining. The referral bonuses are openly described as tied to introductions and business volume. That is enough to identify a commercial offer and a referral plan, but not enough to determine from this video whether the stated services are delivered or how any claimed coin value is realized. The question is not whether the speaker's profit promise is credible; it is whether the cited presentation alone proves that the described transaction has no underlying product or service.

citations.quote: When you become a member of one coin and purchase your trading package, you get access to a
comprehensive training program called the one academy.
five education packages available, all of which contain tokens which you can then exchange to buy mining slots for producing OneCoins
your package includes the cost of mining for coins
Matching bonuses up to 25% are also paid down through 4 generations of referrals.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a paid package, mining claim, and multigeneration bonuses. Those points establish what is being advertised, but do not show whether training or mining slots are actually provided. Nor does a stated bonus on referral business volume alone show that the package consists solely of recruitment. The profit promise is the prosecution's strongest evidence; it is an advertised assertion, not evidence within the video of an actual payout mechanism or its outcome.

citations.quote: comprehensive training program called the one academy.
Onecoin also uses the very popular binary system, and you'll be paid 10% of the business volume generated on your weaker leg.
so whatever happens you will profit from one coin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is what the video promotes, not whether an outside investigation has established delivery or traced payouts. Here, payment buys a package said to include mining; the speaker guarantees profit even without referrals, while also advertising binary and multigeneration bonuses. Calling those components training and commerce does not remove the paid-return promise at the center of the pitch.
